sections.title: Proof checking, proof search, and decision

opening: Quantum computing proposes a new model of computation. When the idea of computation was being developed, it was necessary to define it purely as a sequence of logical operations. As computation is done by a physical device, this process has to be physical. Since quantum mechanics describes all physical processes, computation becomes quantum mechanical. How, then, does this differ from our usual notion of computing devices? To understand this, this chapter builds the necessary ideas leading up to a quantum model of computation.
opening_continuation: We first define what computation is and describe the various models of computation and their limits. We then introduce reversible computation, which paves the way for quantum computation.
intro_continuation: For example, fix your domain to be the set of integers. Your axioms are all the axioms about integers (known as Peano's axioms of arithmetic). Let's make the statement, "The sum of two even integers is even." Starting with \(2a\) and \(2b\), the axioms allow us to write \(2a + 2b = 2(a + b)\), which shows that the sum is even. So, we are able to settle this question. Can we settle all statements that one can frame about integers?
